meta.pattern: NEET-PG 2026 (NBEMS bulletin, 1 Jul 2026): 180 MCQs, 5 sections × 36, 42 min each, sections lock, +4 / −1. The NEET-PG 2027 bulletin is not out yet (expected mid-2027); reports expect the 2026 structure to continue.
meta.official: NBEMS does not publish the question paper or a subject-wise question count. All PYQ data below comes from memory-based recalls compiled by coaching platforms and candidates.
trends: Clinical, application-based questions dominate; long vignettes with close options (2025 and 2026 reports).
Repeats: coaching analyses of 2023-2025 claim about 30% of questions are direct or modified repeats of earlier topics.
Image questions vary a lot by year: about 18-25% claimed for 2025 by PrepLadder (about 50% by another recall blog), but candidates reported very few image questions in 2026.
Video questions: none reported in NEET PG 2026.
Basic sciences are increasingly asked inside clinical scenarios (nerve injuries, enzyme defects, applied physiology).
meta.imageSources: NBEMS does not say where images come from. Reports describe classic, textbook-style images: ECGs, peripheral smears, chest and bone X-rays, CT, CTG and obstetric USG, histopathology slides, gross specimens, clinical photographs (skin, eye, ENT), instruments and specimens. Practise recognising the classic appearance of each, not rare variants.

sources.what: NEET-PG 2026 Information Bulletin: pattern and marking
Older NBE 300-question syllabus weightage (reproduced by DigiNerve, Nov 2025), scaled here to 180
PrepLadder, Most Expected Topics for NEET PG 2026 (PYQ analysis 2023-2025)
MedExamsPrep, NEET PG 2025 recall analysis (its table totals 195 of 200, so treat as approximate)
Fornix Academy, NEET PG 2026 exam analysis (31 Aug 2026)

an.img: Cross-sectional anatomy, nerve-injury hand/limb postures, surface anatomy photos, CT/MRI landmarks
hot: Nerve injury with fracture site; claw hand, wrist drop, ape thumb; Erb and Klumpke palsy
Roots, trunks, cords; branches and their muscles
Trendelenburg sign; gluteal injection site; hip blood supply
Foot drop; knee ligaments and menisci; arches of the foot
Laryngeal nerves and muscles; piriform fossa
Arch derivatives and nerves; pouch derivatives
Coronary dominance; venous drainage; conduction system supply
an.how: Learn every nerve as a clinical picture: site of injury → muscles lost → deformity → sensory loss. Use diagrams and cross-sections, and solve image questions.
an.skip: Detailed origins and insertions of minor muscles, and rare embryological anomalies, beyond the classic ones.

ph.img: ECG strips, pressure-volume loops, O2 dissociation curve, spirometry graphs
hot: JVP waves; heart sounds; pressure-volume loops
O2 dissociation curve shifts; CO poisoning
ph.how: Understand graphs (cardiac cycle, O2 curve, pressure-volume loops) well enough to redraw them. Most questions are applied: what happens to X when Y changes.
ph.skip: Historical experiments, and numerical values that are never clinically used.

bc.img: Electrophoresis patterns, chromatography, clinical photos of metabolic disease
hot: GSD types with enzyme and key feature
Thiamine, B12, folate deficiency and tests
Vitamin A, D, K functions and deficiency
bc.how: Learn each disorder as enzyme → blocked step → what accumulates → clinical clue. Make one table per pathway.
bc.skip: Full structural formulas, and every intermediate of long pathways (learn the rate-limiting and regulated steps).

pa.img: Histopathology slides, gross specimens, peripheral smears, bone marrow
hot: Oncogenes and tumour suppressors; tumour markers; psammoma bodies
Reversible vs irreversible injury; necrosis types; apoptosis
AML M3 t(15;17); CML t(9;22); cytochemistry
Follicular t(14;18), Burkitt t(8;14), Hodgkin RS cells
Peripheral smear findings; HS; thalassaemia vs iron deficiency
pa.how: Pair every disease with its image (slide or smear) and its genetic or marker association. Practise image questions on slides and smears.
pa.skip: Rare tumour subtypes and grading minutiae beyond what has been asked before.

pm.img: Rarely image-based; occasionally drug-reaction photos (SJS, gum hypertrophy)
hot: Azoles vs amphotericin; HIV and hepatitis drugs
Drug of choice by seizure type; teratogenicity
Metformin, SGLT2, GLP-1 actions and side effects
pm.how: Learn drug of choice, mechanism, signature adverse effect and antidote for each group. Recent guideline changes are asked often.
pm.skip: Exact doses (except a few classic ones such as MgSO4 regimens), and brand names.

mi.img: Gram/ZN stains, culture plates and colony morphology, fungal KOH mounts, parasite eggs and smears
hot: Specific media for specific organisms (highest-yield per PL)
Staph vs Strep tests (CAMP, bacitracin, optochin)
mi.how: Image-heavy subject: learn the look of each stain, colony, hypha and egg. Tabulate media, special tests and serology.
mi.skip: Taxonomy history, and rare organisms without a classic clinical picture.

fm.img: Injury photos (bruise ageing, firearm wounds, ligature marks), poisonous plants and snakes, weapons, skull and bone
hot: Rigor, livor, algor mortis; adipocere, mummification
Range of fire; entry vs exit
fm.how: Use photographs for injuries and poisons. Note: India's criminal laws changed on 1 July 2024 (BNS, BNSS, BSA), so check which section numbers your source uses.
fm.skip: Exhaustive lists of old IPC section numbers, and rare poisons.

cm.img: Vaccine vial monitors, vectors (mosquitoes, flies), charts and graphs, cold-chain equipment
hot: Cohort, case-control, RCT, cluster RCT; biases
NTEP, malaria and other national programme updates
cm.how: Biostatistics and epidemiology need practice problems. National programmes change often: always use the latest version (Park's newest edition, plus MoHFW updates).
cm.skip: Historical dates of old programmes, and memorising every guideline number that is never asked.

en.img: Otoscopy photos, audiograms, instruments, X-ray/CT of sinuses
en.how: Learn instruments and the classic otoscopy and audiogram images. Short subject, high return per hour.
en.skip: Operative step-by-step details of rare surgeries.

op.img: Fundus photos, slit-lamp images, visual-field charts, squint photos
hot: Acute angle closure; drugs to avoid
op.how: Image-driven subject: learn the classic fundus and slit-lamp pictures. Draw the visual pathway with each lesion's field defect.
op.skip: Detailed optics calculations beyond the basics.

me.img: ECGs, chest X-rays, peripheral smears, CT brain, clinical signs
hot: ECG diagnosis; AF, heart blocks, SVT management
me.how: Think in management algorithms (first step, drug of choice, next best step). Learn ECG and X-ray patterns from images. Follow the current guideline versions.
me.skip: Rare syndromes with no exam history, and outdated treatment regimens.

su.img: Abdominal X-rays, CT abdomen, clinical photos (swellings, ulcers), instruments
hot: GCS; EDH vs SDH; diffuse axonal injury
su.how: Combine anatomy, imaging and the decision (operate or not). Learn named signs and laws with their meaning. Practise X-ray and CT recognition.
su.skip: Detailed operative steps of rarely asked procedures, and instrument trivia beyond the common ones.

ob.img: CTG traces, obstetric USG, partograph, instruments, specimens
hot: Atonic PPH steps; uterotonics; Bakri balloon (every year per PL)
Partograph, shoulder dystocia (McRoberts), cord prolapse, CTG
AUB evaluation, PCOS, POI (high FSH, low AMH)
Cervical screening, staging, ovarian tumour markers
ob.how: Learn emergencies as stepwise algorithms. CTG and USG images are frequent. One of the highest-weight subjects in recent recalls.
ob.skip: Rare congenital anomalies of the genital tract beyond the classic ones.

pe.img: Clinical photos of syndromes and rashes, growth charts, X-rays (e.g. rickets)
hot: Milestones by age (every year per PL)
Apgar, NRP, early vs late-onset sepsis
Measles, rubella and other rash illnesses
pe.how: Milestones and the immunisation schedule appear almost every year: learn them cold. Use photos for syndromes and rashes.
pe.skip: Rare inborn errors already covered in Biochemistry.

or.img: Fracture X-rays, bone-tumour X-rays, clinical deformity photos
hot: Neck of femur fractures, Garden classification
or.how: X-ray recognition is key: learn the classic fracture and tumour images. Use eponyms with their pictures.
or.skip: Implant brand details and complex fixation techniques.

de.img: Clinical photographs of classic lesions (per PL)
de.how: Almost entirely photo recognition: go through a good image atlas repeatedly. Pair each lesion with one sign and one drug.

hot: Clozapine monitoring; NMS vs serotonin syndrome
ps.how: Short subject: drug side effects and defence mechanisms are classic. Learn DSM-5/ICD-11 key criteria only.

as.img: Airway equipment, laryngoscopy views, capnography traces, circuits
hot: Blood:gas coefficients; MAC; agent of choice
Compression rate and depth; shockable rhythms
as.how: Learn equipment images and capnography patterns. Most questions are drug comparisons.

ra.img: X-ray, CT and MRI signs (the subject itself is images)
hot: SAH, EDH vs SDH on CT
Units, dose limits, most radiosensitive tissues
ra.how: Learn named signs with an image beside each. Radiation units and limits are easy marks.
